current_bottleneck: The deterministic latent path autoencoder is capped: increasing latent capacity from 96 to 256 improves local move reconstruction but still fails validation level occupancy, mean reversion, and pathwise jump geometry in an oracle reconstruction setting.
last_result_summary: 478 trained a larger latent path autoencoder (latent_dim 256, ae_hidden 768) and evaluated reconstruction-oracle geometry. It improved IV MAE to 0.0160, score std ratio to 0.867, daily-change std ratio to 0.702, and daily KS to 21/25, but level KS stayed 10/25, median-bias fell to 15/25, MR ratio was 1.59 with active pass 25%, and pathwise max-jump KS remained 0.875. The deterministic autoencoder form remains below deployable geometry before conditional sampling.
next_step_recommendation: Run post-experiment analysis and close or reframe the deterministic latent-manifold branch. Do not sweep latent dimension, decoder width, flow temperature, or add calibration; the next viable move likely requires a different paradigm than deterministic future-path compression.
current_best_note: Ties the official revised-suite 8/11 frontier with better residual geometry than 385a: level KS 10/25, median-bias fraction 20/25, bias magnitude 25/25, daily KS 25/25, conditionality pass, and cointegration pass. Architecture is unchanged; the change is a theoretically proper free-running path-energy score fine-tune anchored by FM.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
